design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller wants one ordinary thing: the request she already made for two more days put back in front of the host, with a price on it. Nothing she says touches the two numbers the desk must produce. The first is a debt the records already owe and nobody has raised — the young-driver surcharge on a 23-year-old driver — and the agent has to notice it from the profile and the reserved dates, then work out a rate that four separate rules move off its standard reading. The second is the quote itself, which the pricing rule refuses to fix until that surcharge stands on the reservation, and which is then priced on the time the lapsed request asked for rather than on the plan's maximum. The difficulty is in reading the policy, reconciling the reservation's own lines and readings and its protection election in another product, and getting two figures exactly right; an agent that reads only the two computation documents produces 139.39 and 285.12, confidently and wrongly, and an agent that lodges the request before raising the surcharge quotes 177.04.

SCOPE. Already occupied by task 0: trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant and trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing, with the tools grant_mileage_topup_0373887d and pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94 — the mid-trip mileage top-up, its granting and its pricing. This task claims trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge and trips_ext_extension_quote, with post_young_driver_surcharge_8e3312c3 and submit_extension_request_8f69bfd6 — the surcharge owed on the reserved period itself and the quoting of extra time onto the extension request register. The two scopes share no policy, no tool and no computed quantity: task 0 computes miles granted and the price of bought miles, this one computes a surcharge on the reserved period and the price of extra time. Both raise lines on the same base event, trips_reservation_charge_posted, but under different bases (extra_miles_package against young_driver_surcharge), through different tools, and neither reads the other's records. With the two tasks of this difficulty closed, every extended policy is claimed exactly once; nothing is left reserved.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk --tasks 2` printed for this task: {"task": 1, "key": "env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. The tree carries exactly one prerequisite problem besides the root, and each computation carries five declared factors: trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge five, trips_ext_extension_quote five.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: trips_ext_extension_quote — what the caller asks for is the request going back to the host with a price on it. Prerequisite problem: trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge. One edge, from the quote to the surcharge.
  kind: value_input. gate: the compute binding yd_share of the quote policy.
  form: state. The prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the quote policy's own rule, is "A quote for extra time is not fixed before the reservation carries the young-driver surcharge owed on the driver named on it."
  Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result (a quote for extra time) to what it waits on with the ordering connective "not ... before"; (2) its far side is a record-visible state — a young-driver surcharge carried among the reservation's priced lines, which the trip charge lookup shows — and it names no action, no performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no snake_case or hex token; (4) it is written at exactly the strength of the edge, a hard requirement scoped to the surcharge owed on the driver named on this reservation and nothing wider. The negated direction is the one this desk would use, because a quote is a thing that is not given until what it rests on stands; the other policy of this difficulty that carries a prerequisite sentence states it in the affirmative direction, and the two were chosen sentence by sentence rather than by alternation.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: raising the young-driver surcharge line, which is what trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge's rule provides for; no other policy in this charter puts a surcharge of that kind on a reservation. Derivation: the sentence says the quote waits on a young-driver surcharge standing on the reservation; the trip charge lookup shows a base rate, a marketplace fee, a deposit and a goodwill credit and no such line; the surcharge policy's rule states what that line comes to and that it is raised as its own line. One action follows, the one recorded as resolved_by.
  Why it does not hold at the opening: the four charge rows seeded on the reservation carry charge_basis base_rate, trip_fee, deposit and goodwill_refund; none is young_driver_surcharge, while the guest's date of birth of 2002-11-30 puts her at 23 on the first day of the reserved period, so the surcharge is owed and unraised.
  Topological order: trips_ext_young_driver_surcharge, then trips_ext_extension_quote. Nothing stands in parallel.
  Per-edge deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): with the surcharge write skipped, the quote's surcharge share falls from 15.49 to nil and the scored quoted_amount from 192.53 to 177.04, and the terminal records carry neither the surcharge line nor the right price on the register.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject trips_reservation_charge_posted. Governing base policies: trips_evt_reservation_pricing and trips_evt_payment_recovery. The pricing policy's eligibility booking_open_for_pricing applies: "a line is posted only while the reservation is in the requested, booked or in_progress state". At frozen_time the reservation is in_progress, so it holds; once it settles the line could not be raised at all and a reversal would be the only route. One clause of that base policy is superseded, and the policy's overwrite names it: "pays the young-driver surcharge on the discounted base rate" is replaced by "The surcharge is the effective surcharge rate taken on the amount charged over, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end.", because this policy settles the surcharge at a rate that moves with the reservation's own standing and on an amount apportioned over the days charged rather than at the plan's flat percentage of the discounted base rate. Without that declaration base's fifteen per cent of 1084.16 and this policy's ten per cent of the same figure would both stand, and one guest would owe two different surcharges. Everything else of that base policy is inherited as written and is the ground of this one: the surcharge is owed by a driver under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period, it is posted as its own line so that it can be reversed on its own, and the locked daily rate is the basis of every later line. trips_evt_payment_recovery carries no structured eligibility for this write and is recorded as policy_scope. No time gate governs this write.
  Write 2, subject trips_extension_charge_posted. Governing base policy: trips_evt_extension alone; the recovery policy's subject list does not carry this event. Its eligibility extension_decision_window is a time gate: "The extension is priced only where the host's decision is recorded no later than the decision window counted forward from the scheduled return of the reservation." Anchor event: the host's decision is recorded. Authoritative anchor: trips_bookings.trip_end_date = 2026-09-18. Direction: not_after. Duration: params.extension_decision_window_hours, three hours on the Weekly plan. Unit: elapsed hours, counted in whole elapsed hours from the scheduled return, an hour counting only once fully elapsed. Boundary: inclusive. At the frozen clock of 2026-09-16 09:05 UTC the window has not even opened its last hour, so pricing is in time; the positive and negative boundary cases are written out in temporal_feasibility. One clause of that base policy is superseded, and the policy's overwrite names it: "Extended time is priced at the locked daily rate lifted by the plan's uplift percentage, applied to the extended days only" is replaced by the sentence that lifts the locked daily rate by the extension uplift this policy settles, because the uplift a guest is quoted turns on what has already happened to their earlier request rather than being the plan's flat figure. Without that declaration the plan's published eight per cent and this policy's four per cent would both stand on the same two days. The rest of the policy is inherited: the request goes onto the register rather than onto the reservation, the reservation's scheduled return moves only on the host's approval, the lead time is at least twelve hours before the scheduled return on this plan (the request is lodged two days before), one extension may not add more than the plan's maximum additional hours and several are added together against it (48 hours asked against a 72-hour maximum), and a declined or expired request leaves the reservation untouched. The register lodgement charge is not the fee base publishes for changing the dates of a confirmed booking: lodging a request moves no date, and the rule says so in terms, so the two never price the same act and nothing is superseded there.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object is the guest's only reservation, ee1d196c-62b5-489c-874b-2dbcf899e804, Weekly plan, in progress 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-18. Correlation key: booking_id, carried by every charge line, every usage row, the extension request and the protection election. Rows entering the aggregates: the base-rate line of 1084.16 and the deposit line for the surcharge; the allowance grant of 1225 and the two odometer readings of -620 and -380 for the conduct adjustment; the lapsed extension request for the uplift, the quoted time and the lodgement charge; the 728.00 daily protection fee line for both protection tiers. Rows excluded and why, with what folding each in actually does, recomputed one substitution at a time: the 109.20 young-driver protection surcharge on the election, which the rule excludes because only daily protection fee lines count toward the eight-hundred-dollar band - folding it in reaches 837.20, flips the protection adjustment from two points to four and the cover credit from 9.00 to 14.00 a day, and gives 86.73 and 182.53 instead of 108.42 and 192.53; and the goodwill credit of -25.00, which is raised against the marketplace fee and not the base-rate line - netting it into the base-rate line the surcharge is spread over gives a daily base of 75.65, an amount charged over of 1059.10 and 105.91 instead of 108.42. Those are the two near-misses this task claims, and both are recomputed. The fuel reading taken at collection books no miles and is filtered out by event type, so folding it in changes nothing, and it is not claimed as one.

WORLD, ROW BY ROW. The customer row carries the date of birth that makes the surcharge owed at all and the driver score of 74 that both meets the Weekly plan's entry score and keeps the deposit line legitimate below the plan's waiver score of 80. The booking carries the in_progress status the pricing gate reads, the fourteen-day reserved period that lifts two of the surcharge tiers, the actual start equal to the first reserved day that decides the days-charged anchor, the locked daily rate the extension uplift is taken on, and the allowance figures. The four charge lines carry the base the surcharge is taken on, the deposit the rate tier reads, and the excluded goodwill credit. The four usage rows carry the allowance and the two readings whose 1000 miles sit between three quarters of 1225 and 1225 itself - delete either reading and the conduct adjustment falls away - plus the excluded fuel reading. The lapsed extension request is the load-bearing row of the root problem: it is what makes the uplift 4 per cent rather than 8, what the extra time is taken from, and the one request already standing that makes the lodgement charge 12.00 rather than nothing. The protection election and its two lines are the cross-difficulty evidence for three tiers across the two computations, and both lines are what the guestplan charter produces for the level elected: Keyturn Premier Protection charges the greater of 52.00 a day and 45 per cent of the trip price, billed at trip start, so fourteen days of cover come to 728.00 against 487.87 on the percentage basis, that being 45 per cent of the reservation's base-rate line of 1084.16, and the daily figure stands; that level's young-driver protection surcharge is 15 per cent, which is the 109.20 line raised on a guest of 23; and it charges nothing for a declared additional driver, which is why the one declared driver carries no fee line. The election's coverage_days of 14 and its protection_fee_balance_due of 837.20 are the days charged and the sum of the two lines. No automatic clause of the base charter is lit: nothing is late, nothing is unpaid past its retries, no mileage or fuel settlement is due before the return, and the reservation is not near its cancellation or no-show boundaries. The same standing constraint holds on any reseed here: the ledger sums take the readings as booked, so no two readings may cover the same handover; the two on this reservation are dated 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-15 and no two cover one, so base's rule that a telematics reading is authoritative over a host or guest one never has to break a tie and nothing is overridden.

PERSONA. Tessa is younger, busier and more clipped than the caller of task 0, and the text is organised around a person mid-move rather than around a checklist: she opens with the whole story in two sentences, gives her name and mobile because that is how she starts, and parts with the rest of her details only as the agent needs them. Her one disclaimer is about the trip's dates and nothing else - she does not want them moved today - and she says in terms that what the trip has or has not been billed for she leaves to the desk, so nothing she says bears on whether the surcharge the records already owe is raised. She knows what she asked for and that it went stale, which is a fact the register carries; she does not know what extra time costs, what her age has to do with anything, or what protection level she chose, and she says so rather than guessing. Her reactions are conditional but unscripted: she accepts the figure when it is given, lodges the request herself once it is handed over, and closes when she hears it is in front of the host — exactly where evaluation_criteria closes.

REACHABILITY IN A REAL CONVERSATION. She states the mobile and name the profile is found from and two more details for the identity check; the booking lookup gives the reservation and its dates; the charge lookup shows what stands on it and, by its absence, what does not; the usage lookup gives the allowance and readings; the extension register gives the lapsed request, its hours and its requested date; the two protection lookups give the election and its fees. The agent raises the surcharge, quotes the extra time, she agrees, the agent unlocks the request and hands it over, she lodges it. Every question a real agent would ask has an answer in the persona, including the ones that never enter gold; the one thing she cannot supply, her booking reference, is written as a refusal with the obvious consequence. Nothing waits on the host's decision — the request is lodged and left standing, which is exactly what the base rule says a request does — and nothing waits on a bank, a workshop or a future date. Both writes land under one frozen clock.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG. Quoting the extra time before raising the surcharge (177.04). Taking the standard 15 per cent rate and ignoring the deposit-secured long period (173.47). Missing the protection relief (130.10) or the conduct point (97.57) or the declared driver (86.73). Charging the surcharge over the days run so far instead of the reserved period (92.93). Counting the 109.20 young-driver protection surcharge toward the eight-hundred-dollar protection band, which takes four points off instead of two and gives 86.73 on the surcharge and 182.53 on the quote. Netting the goodwill credit into the base-rate line the surcharge is spread over (105.91). On the quote: taking the standard 8 per cent uplift (199.57), quoting the plan's maximum 72 hours instead of the 48 the lapsed request asked for (282.79), forgetting the lodgement charge (180.53) or the cover credit on the extended days (210.53). Every one of these is excluded by the rule text read against the records.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the member, verify her, read the reservation, its lines, its readings, its extension register and its protection election. Compute the surcharge: 9 per cent for a fourteen-day period with a deposit standing, less 2 for an active Premier election whose daily protection fees come to 728.00 and so fall short of the eight-hundred-dollar band, plus 1 for driving between three quarters and all of the allowance, plus 2 for the declared additional driver, giving 10 per cent; fourteen days charged from the first reserved day to the scheduled return; 1084.16 over fourteen days is 77.44 a day and fourteen days make 1084.16; 10 per cent of that is 108.42. Raise it. Then compute the quote: 4 per cent uplift on 88.00 is 91.52, two extended days make 183.04; the surcharge share is 108.42 over fourteen days for two days, 15.49; the lodgement charge is 12.00 on one request already standing; the cover credit is 9.00 a day for two days, 18.00, taken off; the quote is 192.53. Unlock the request, hand it over, and she lodges it to 2026-09-20 for 48.0 hours at that price.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The handling-time recomputation was run from the policies on disk with the gates' own evaluator (build_env / eval_compute / substitute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) over this initial_state, with the surcharge write simulated before the quote. Output: "B surcharge result= 108.42" with factor baselines 173.47, 130.1, 97.57, 86.73, 92.93 and an all-baseline fall-back of 139.39; "A quote result= 192.53" with factor baselines 199.57, 282.79, 177.04, 180.53, 210.53 and an all-baseline fall-back of 285.12; and the prerequisite-sensitivity run "A quote WITHOUT B result= 177.04". The two claimed near-misses were recomputed the same way: counting the young-driver protection surcharge as a protection fee gives 86.73 and 182.53, and netting the goodwill credit into the base-rate line the surcharge is spread over gives a daily base of 75.65, an amount charged over of 1059.10 and 105.91. Every figure equals the declared expected, baseline_result and factor_sensitivity entries, and the gold arguments at steps 9 and 11.

RULE AGAINST COMPUTE, BOTH WAYS. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis — the counts and sums over the reservation's own lines, readings and register, the three cross-category reads, each ladder, the effective rate, the day counts, the apportionment and the final rounding. Backward: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed. The surcharge rule's sentences on what the surcharge is, what it is charged over, the standard values and how the adjustments combine are claimed by result, daily_base/charged_base, the factor baselines and effective_rate; its five ladder paragraphs by surcharge_rate, protection_adjustment, conduct_adjustment, driver_adjustment and days_charged. The quote rule's sentences on what the quote is, the price of extended time, the standard values and the five ladders are claimed by result, uplifted_daily/extension_price/extended_days and the five ladder bindings; the lodgement branch tests exactly the two conditions its sentence and its ladder state, the number of requests already standing, and nothing else, so prose and expression select the same charge on every world and not merely on this one. Semantic choices are pinned in prose: the adjustments are stated to be in percentage points and all added to the rate before the rate is taken on anything (never applied one after another to the money); the amount charged over is stated to be the base-rate line spread evenly over the reserved days and taken per day charged; the day counts state their endpoints ("the day of return counted", "with that day counted"); the rounding is stated to happen once at the end on each computed line; and the extended days are stated to be rounded up to the next whole day with a floor of one.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. The surcharge write carries both base policies governing its subject, with the pricing gate quoted verbatim and satisfied by the reservation's in_progress status correlated on booking_id, and its stage fact is preexisting_before_conversation, cited to the guest's date of birth and the first reserved day - the debt exists in the records before the call and the call only books it. The quote write carries trips_evt_extension with its time gate, cited to frozen_time, the scheduled return, and the lapsed request's status and reference, with the boundary cases written out; its stage fact is established_by_prior_tool, citing step 9, which is the only honest reading. No status registration anywhere stands in for an event outside the conversation: the host's decision is not registered, not assumed and not waited for - the request is left standing exactly as the base rule says it stands.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computations, gold and this dossier masked, and working only from the prose of the two policies as they will be published, the two tool schemas, what the lookups return on this world and what the persona says, the same two numbers come out in the same order: 108.42 raised on the reservation, then 192.53 lodged with a request to 2026-09-20 for 48.0 hours, handed to the customer to lodge. The places a second reading might have arisen are settled outright by the rule text: which amount the surcharge is charged over (the base-rate line spread over the reserved days, not the balance and not the line net of the credit against the fee), which extra time is quoted (the time the lapsed request asked for, not the plan's maximum), which lines count as protection fees (the daily ones, not the young-driver surcharge raised on the same election), and, since each departure from base is named in an overwrite that quotes the clause it replaces, which of base's figures still stand.

REVISIONS. (1) Round 1. The quote was first drafted to price the extra time the caller named in conversation; symptom: the figure would have rested on a number only the persona carried, which the compute cannot read and which would have made the quote depend on the simulator rather than the records. Root cause: the quantity was sourced from speech, not from the world. Change: the lapsed request on the extension register became the source of the extra time, with the rule stating that a fresh quote after a request has expired is priced on the time that request asked for; the caller now asks for "the same two extra days" and the register supplies 48.0 hours and 2026-09-20. Re-run: the quote recomputes at 241.43 and both non-computed arguments gained an exclusive documentary basis. (2) Round 1. The additional-driver fee was added to the protection election as a near-miss after the first draft had only protection fee lines, so that the hundred-dollar floor tests a filter rather than a bare total; the seed_consistency and factor traces record the exclusion. (8) Round 5, after the source audit's revision 4. The one red was F-07, and it is the same class as round 4's B-1 with its sign reversed: change_count counts every row of the extension request register, and the prose said only 'where one extension request already stands on the reservation' - a positive-sounding phrase that names no status, next to two sibling counts whose status filters the prose does name, and against base's inherited clause that a declined or expired request leaves the reservation untouched. A reader could therefore count nothing and charge nothing. Route taken: the prose moves, not the compute, because the compute's reading is the one the charge was re-scoped to in round 3 - it answers to the burden of a fresh request landing on a register that already holds others, and lodging a request is expressly not something that touches the reservation. So the count is now taken over the extension request register rather than over the reservation, and the rule says in terms that a request stands on the register whatever has become of it, naming all six states the register can hold. No overwrite is declared and none is owed: base's clause is about what a declined or expired request does to the reservation, which this rule agrees with and now cites as the very reason the count is taken over the register instead. No compute expression was touched and no scored value moved. The sweep was then re-run with the negative case added - for every aggregate, which filter it does NOT impose that a reader could assume, taken from the union of filters its siblings impose on the same table plus that table's own status and kind dimensions. Nineteen bindings carry at least one such dimension. Those now pinned in prose: what counts as an odometer reading (a fuel or battery reading is not one, whatever odometer figure it notes - which closes O-13) and that every reading counts whoever took it, since a reading another supersedes books no miles and so adds nothing, which states base's telematics and post-trip-audit rules where this sum meets them; that miles granted count whatever they were granted for; that a line once raised for a mileage overage, and a deposit line, count however they were afterwards treated; that the amount the surcharge is charged over is the base-rate lines as raised, a credit or reversal against one being a line of its own and not taken off it; that every young-driver surcharge line standing is taken together; and that the daily protection fees count however many lines they stand as and whenever they were raised. Adjudicated as not assumable and left unstated, with the reasoning recorded: billing_period and payment_channel on the charge ledger, and coverage_segment and adjustment_reason on the other product's ledger - none of these identifies the line the rule names, and the kind restriction that does is already stated. Nothing further. O-14 is answered in two parts. The half that base settles - two readings covering one handover - is no longer an invariant but a sentence of the rule, since a superseded reading books no miles. The half that remains is the LATEST tie: two mileage readings sharing a usage_date, which cannot be broken in business words because the evaluator breaks it by row order. No gate inside this difficulty's write domain can enforce it, so it is now checked mechanically by the authoring sweeper on every run, which reports 'world invariants hold: no LATEST tie, no two readings on one handover' for both tasks of this difficulty, and the check is re-run whenever either world changes. (7) Round 4, after the render-layer audit. Symptom: read from the published documents alone this task's two scored values came out at 86.73 and 179.44 against 108.42 and 192.53. Two source-side gaps caused it, both of them rule/compute non-equivalence of the class round 2 closed as F-05. First (B-1 / P-1): the fee limb of the protection adjustment and of the cover credit reads only the election's daily protection fee lines in compute and in inputs.history, while the prose said only 'the protection fees charged on it' - so the documents directed a reader to take 728.00 and 109.20 together, 837.20, and cross the eight-hundred-dollar band the source keeps below it. The prose now reads 'the daily protection fees charged on it' in every sentence, every ladder tier and every quotation of both policies, and the tier sentences name what is excluded, the young-driver protection surcharge among them - which is exactly the near-miss this task turns on, so the documents can now carry both the rule and the trap. Second (B-4 / P-5): the share ladder said only 'spread evenly over the days of the reserved period and taken for each extended day', leaving the renderer to invent a per-day rounding that costs a cent; the compute rounds once, after the spreading and the taking, and the ladder now says so in both tiers and states that the reserved period runs from its first day to its last, both counted. A sweep of every binding of all four policies against its prose then pinned the rest of the class here: the counting convention behind 'how long the trip has run'; the two roundings the amount charged over passes through; the rounding of the lifted daily rate, of the price of the extended time and of the cover credit; and which of several expired or declined requests is read, now stated as the latest by the time it was put on the register. No compute expression was touched and no scored value moved: 108.42 and 192.53, every factor figure and every baseline unchanged. (6) Round 3. The audit found one false proof figure: computations[0].factor_trace asserted that a reader who nets the goodwill credit into the base-rate line reaches 106.62, a figure left behind when the effective rate moved from eight to ten per cent. Recomputed at the moment that sentence names, the rule spreads the netted line over the reserved days - a daily base of 75.65 and an amount charged over of 1059.10 - and ten per cent of it is 105.91; netting at the charged-base step instead gives 105.92, and no reading reaches 106.62. The near-miss is real at 105.91 and the scored value is unaffected. A mechanical stale-figure sweep was then written and run over both task files, checking every number in every proof field against the figures the world, the charter and every replay variant make true, including the near-miss substitutions the dossiers claim; it found the same false figure in two further places in this design_rationale, which the audit had not reached, and both are corrected. Four figures remain outside the machine-checkable set and are adjudicated by hand across the two files: 241.43 here, which is revision 1's gold reported by change-log entry (1) and true of the moment it names; 487.87, now stated as 45 per cent of the reservation's base-rate line of 1084.16; and two in task 0's file. No other assertion in this file is false of the world it names. (3) Round 2, after the source-layer audit. Symptom: this task had further defensible answers on both scored parameters, because the surcharge replaced base's young-driver rate and acting base and the quote replaced the plan's extension uplift, both with overwrite: [] (findings F-03, F-04 / 1-A, 1-B); the lodgement charge was written as a date-change fee against base's published date-change terms, which the policy neither cited nor overrode (F-05b / 1-C); and the compute branch for that charge carried a seven-day conjunct that neither its rule sentence nor its ladder stated (F-05). Change: the surcharge policy's overwrite now names and replaces "pays the young-driver surcharge on the discounted base rate", the quote policy's overwrite names and replaces "Extended time is priced at the locked daily rate lifted by the plan's uplift percentage, applied to the extended days only", the fee became a register lodgement charge of 24.00 / 12.00 / nothing with a rule sentence stating in terms that lodging a request changes no date and is therefore not what base's date-change terms price, and the stray conjunct is gone so that rule, ladder and compute select the same charge on every world. Re-run: the scored figures move to 108.42 and 192.53 and every sensitivity figure with them. (4) Round 2, the cross-difficulty evidence and the near-misses (F-06 / 1-D). Symptom: the seeded protection rows charged 9.00 a day on a level whose charter daily flat is 52.00 and carried a 45.00 secondary-driver fee on a level that charges nothing for one, and two of the three near-misses the dossier claimed could not change any figure. Change: the election now carries one charter-correct daily protection fee line of 728.00 for fourteen days and one young-driver protection surcharge of 109.20, which is 15 per cent of it and exactly what Keyturn Premier Protection charges a guest of 23; the impossible secondary-driver row is gone; the protection band moved from one hundred to eight hundred dollars and the ladder gained a second relief tier, so the correct total of 728.00 lands on the lower relief and counting the 109.20 line flips it - a near-miss that moves both scored numbers. The fuel-reading and secondary-driver near-miss claims are withdrawn. Re-run: 86.73 and 182.53 under the near-miss against 108.42 and 192.53 in gold. (5) Round 2, the protection charge on extended days became a cover credit: charging a guest a protection amount inside a trips quote set a price against guestplan's published daily protection fee, which this difficulty may not do; the quote now gives a credit of its own money for a well-covered trip instead, and takes it off the total.
user_scenario:
Tessa Fontaine took a car for a fortnight while she moves flats across Lake Washington, and the move has slipped. She is calling in the middle of a working afternoon, half packing boxes, and she comes to the point quickly: she asked the host last weekend whether she could hang on to the car for two more days, heard nothing back at all, and has since seen that the request went stale. She wants to put the same ask in again, the same two extra days, and she wants to know what the extra time is going to cost her before she commits to it. She is clear that she is not asking for the trip's dates to be moved today - only for the request to go in front of the host again with a price on it, and she will lodge it herself if that is how it is done. What the trip itself has or has not been billed for she leaves to the desk.

She offers her name, Tessa Fontaine, and the mobile she books with, 4255610994, at the start. When the agent wants something more to go on she gives her date of birth, 2002-11-30, and the ZIP of her billing address, 98033; her licence number, 51683042, and her email, tessa.fontaine@northmail.com, come out only if those are not enough. argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_id: The value is the row id of the caller's live reservation. Basis: the trip booking lookup returns one reservation for her, priced under the 'Keyturn Weekly Rate Plan', in progress from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-18, and the tool's contract says the reference number is 'read from the trip booking lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: she holds no other reservation, so no other value is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The value is the member reference number returned by the profile lookup for the caller. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the member reference number of the guest the line is raised against, read from the member profile lookup before the call', and the reservation names that member as its guest. Uniqueness: one profile matches the mobile and name she states.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.surcharge_amount: 108.42 USD. The surcharge is the effective rate taken on the amount charged over. The reserved period runs 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-18, fourteen days, and a deposit line of 400.00 stands on the reservation, so the surcharge rate is 9 per cent. The trip's protection election is written as 'Keyturn Premier Protection' and stands active, and the daily protection fees charged on it come to 728.00, less than eight hundred dollars, so two percentage points come off rather than four; the 109.20 young-driver protection surcharge raised on the same election is not a daily protection fee and does not count toward that total, and counting it would reach 837.20 and take four points off instead. The allowance granted to the reservation is 1225 miles and its two readings have booked 620 + 380 = 1000 miles, more than three quarters of 1225 but not more than it, with the trip eleven days run, so one percentage point goes on. One additional driver is declared on the election and the reserved period runs fourteen days or more, so two more percentage points go on. The effective rate is 9 - 2 + 1 + 2 = 10 per cent. The trip started on the first day of the reserved period and has run at least seven days, so the days charged run from 2026-09-05 to the scheduled return of 2026-09-18 with the return day counted, fourteen days. The base-rate line of 1084.16 spread over the fourteen reserved days is 77.44 a day, and fourteen days charged make 1084.16. Ten per cent of 1084.16 is 108.42. The goodwill refund of -25.00 sits against the marketplace fee, not the base-rate line, and does not enter.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.quoted_amount: 192.53 USD. The quote is the price of the extended time plus the young-driver share and the register lodgement charge, less the cover credit. A request on this reservation expired without a decision and the trip has run eleven days, so the extension uplift is 4 per cent and the extra time quoted is the 48.0 hours that request asked for, which is two extended days. The locked daily rate of 88.00 lifted by 4 per cent is 91.52, and two extended days make 183.04. A young-driver surcharge of 108.42 now stands on the reservation and the extra time runs to two days or more, so the share is that surcharge spread over the fourteen reserved days and taken for each extended day: 108.42 / 14 x 2 = 15.49. One extension request already stands on the reservation, so the register lodgement charge is 12.00; lodging a request changes no date, so the marketplace's date-change terms do not price it. The trip's protection election stands active and the daily protection fees charged on it come to 728.00, less than eight hundred dollars, so the cover credit is 9.00 for each extended day, 18.00. The quote is 183.04 + 15.49 + 12.00 - 18.00 = 192.53.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Raising the surcharge puts a line of 108.42 with the young-driver basis on the reservation, so the surcharge standing on it becomes 108.42 and the share falling on the two extended days 15.49.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree carries a single edge, so one order is possible: the surcharge is raised and the quote is fixed after it. No two writes stand in parallel, and the quote reads the surcharge through the reservation's priced lines, so no other sequence reaches the same terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying the call without the surcharge line leaves the surcharge standing on the reservation at nothing, so the young-driver share falls from 15.49 to nil and the scored quoted_amount from 192.53 to 177.04; the terminal records also lack the 108.42 surcharge line, and the request lodged on the register carries the wrong price.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks only for her lapsed request for two more days to go back to the host with a price on it. She never mentions a surcharge, never says that anything is missing from her bill, never suggests that something has to be sorted out first, and does not know what her age has to do with the price of anything. What she does say about the trip - when she collected the car, when it is due back, that a friend is a second driver, that protection is charged weekly - is either what the desk would ask her or ordinary talk, and none of it names the surcharge or the order of the writes. The existence of the prerequisite reaches the agent only through the policy sentence that a quote for extra time is not fixed before the reservation carries the young-driver surcharge owed on the driver named on it.
